<details>
<summary>🪧 Tips</summary>

### Chat

There are 3 ways to chat with [CodeRabbit](https://coderabbit.ai):

- Review comments: Directly reply to a review comment made by CodeRabbit. Example:
  - `I pushed a fix in commit <commit_id>, please review it.`
  - `Generate unit testing code for this file.`
  - `Open a follow-up GitHub issue for this discussion.`
- Files and specific lines of code (under the "Files changed" tab): Tag `@coderabbitai` in a new review comment at the desired location with your query. Examples:
  - `@coderabbitai generate unit testing code for this file.`
  -	`@coderabbitai modularize this function.`
- PR comments: Tag `@coderabbitai` in a new PR comment to ask questions about the PR branch. For the best results, please provide a very specific query, as very limited context is provided in this mode. Examples:
  - `@coderabbitai gather interesting stats about this repository and render them as a table. Additionally, render a pie chart showing the language distribution in the codebase.`
  - `@coderabbitai read src/utils.ts and generate unit testing code.`
  - `@coderabbitai read the files in the src/scheduler package and generate a class diagram using mermaid and a README in the markdown format.`
  - `@coderabbitai help me debug CodeRabbit configuration file.`

Note: Be mindful of the bot's finite context window. It's strongly recommended to break down tasks such as reading entire modules into smaller chunks. For a focused discussion, use review comments to chat about specific files and their changes, instead of using the PR comments.

### CodeRabbit Commands (Invoked using PR comments)

- `@coderabbitai pause` to pause the reviews on a PR.
- `@coderabbitai resume` to resume the paused reviews.
- `@coderabbitai review` to trigger an incremental review. This is useful when automatic reviews are disabled for the repository.
- `@coderabbitai full review` to do a full review from scratch and review all the files again.
- `@coderabbitai summary` to regenerate the summary of the PR.
- `@coderabbitai generate docstrings` to [generate docstrings](https://docs.coderabbit.ai/finishing-touches/docstrings) for this PR. ([Beta](https://docs.coderabbit.ai/early-access#beta))
- `@coderabbitai resolve` resolve all the CodeRabbit review comments.
- `@coderabbitai configuration` to show the current CodeRabbit configuration for the repository.
- `@coderabbitai help` to get help.

### Other keywords and placeholders

- Add `@coderabbitai ignore` anywhere in the PR description to prevent this PR from being reviewed.
- Add `@coderabbitai summary` to generate the high-level summary at a specific location in the PR description.
- Add `@coderabbitai` anywhere in the PR title to generate the title automatically.

### CodeRabbit Configuration File (`.coderabbit.yaml`)

- You can programmatically configure CodeRabbit by adding a `.coderabbit.yaml` file to the root of your repository.

issue.body:
## 🔍 개요
+ close #393 

## ✔️ 문제 풀이 진행 사항
올완

## 📝 문제 풀이 전략 및 실제 풀이 방법
- [백준_2146_다리 만들기]
A형 준비할 때 풀었던 기억이..ㅎ
BFS 이용해서 배열에 섬 번호 부여하고, 또 BFS 이용하여 현재 섬과 다른 번호의 섬을 만나는 경우 최솟값을 갱신해주었음!
저는 두 BFS 과정에서 같은 방문 배열을 이용하면서 중간에 초기화를 안해줘서 메모리 초과가 났었습니다.

- [백준_1327_소트 게임]
String 형태의 수열과 뒤집은 횟수를 가지고 BFS를 이용하여 풀었음. 수열을 String으로 변경하여 앞에서부터 k개씩 뒤집어서 새로운 수열을 구해서 큐에 넣어주면서 모든 경우를 탐색함. 
String의 subString을 이용하여 (숫자)+ (뒤집은 숫자)+(숫자) 이런 식으로 합쳐서 새로운 수열을 만들었음. 
초반에 저장해둔 입력 받은 수열의 오름차순과 비교하여 같다면 몇 번째 변경인지 반환하였음. 
이미 만들어졌던 수열인지 확인하기 위해 boolean[] 배열의 인덱스를 수열의 숫자로 가정하고 체크하였음. n의 최댓값이 8이므로 99,999,999 크기로 생성함.

- [백준_2665_미로만들기]
n,m에 도달하기 위해 최소한 교환 해야 하는 방 수를 저장하는 disf[][]배열을 두고 이 배열을 갱신해나갔음.
BFS로 진행하며 다음 칸이 검은 방인 경우에는 방을 바꿔야하므로 dist의 현재 위치 값에 +1을 해주고, 다음 칸이 흰 방이라면 그대로 값을 유지함. 
그 값과 다음 칸의 dist 값을 비교하여 다음 칸이 더 크다면, 더 적은 교환 횟수로 갈 수 있다는 것이므로 값을 치환해줌!
최종적으로 dist[n-1][n-1]칸에 최소 교환 횟수가 저장됨.

## ETC
char[]를 String으로 변경할 때 String.valueOf 는 char 배열 내용 기반으로 String 객체 자체를 새로 만들고,
toString()은 배열 객체의 메모리 위치인 해시 코드 값을 문자열로 반환해준다고 합니다.
String 형태로 배열 내용을 이용해야 할 때는 String.valueOf를 쓰는 것이 조을 듯 합니다.. 

## 🧐 참고 사항

10.4

Improvements

In this release, we have added support for test density and metrics at the individual file level. You can now view the number of unit tests, as well as details on skipped tests, failed tests, and test duration, from all supported coverage tools (xUnit, MsTest, and nUnit).

Additionally, we have significantly optimized memory allocation, resulting in memory usage reduction during registration.

controlled_redelivery.label: Controlled in-memory second pass; not observed source deliveries

limitations: Only first accepted event JSON is retained. Individual duplicate delivery bodies and delivery order are not retained; duplicate counts cannot identify which events repeated.
Rejected content has a hash and reason only. Its exact changed fields cannot be recovered.
Event-time order is a deterministic presentation, not delivery, commit or database CDC order. Stale deliveries, complete history and exactly-once processing cannot be established.
The response hash identifies the original HTTP bytes, which are not retained. It cannot be recomputed from deduplicated bronze. Evidence hashes are fingerprints, not authentication.
The second pass repeats retained identities in memory only; no source fetch, publication, counter update or model call occurs. Checks cover selected acquisitions only.
report.ordering: Event timestamp ascending, then numeric event identity; not source delivery order
report.scope: Selected retained GitHub acquisitions; publication reconstruction, not source CDC
